thread.title: A Push to Remove Facebook CEO Mark Zuckerberg as Chairman Has New Backers

author: Barron's
title: A Push to Remove Facebook CEO Mark Zuckerberg as Chairman Has New Backers
text:
Marlene Awaad/Bloomberg Facebook isn't just facing increasingly skeptical investors and consumers. Three state treasurers and the New York City comptroller have joined a shareholder proposal to strip Chief Executive Mark Zuckerberg of his chairmanship.
The state treasurers of Illinois, Pennsylvania, and Rhode Island, all of whom have public funds with Facebook ( FB ) holdings, and New York City's pension fund, all joined the proposal on Wednesday. It was initially filed by Trillium Asset Management in June. At the time, Trillium listed a litany of reasons, including the Cambridge Analytica data breach , Russian meddling in the 2016 presidential election, the spread of "fake news," and social media addiction. Since then, the group has added a breach in September that affected 30 million Facebook accounts, as well as the departure of Instagram and WhatsApp executives, to its grievances.
"An independent board chair is essential to moving Facebook forward from this mess, and to reestablish trust with Americans and investors alike," New York City Comptroller Scott Stringer said in a statement Wednesday. The fund holds 4.7 million shares in Facebook as of the end of the first quarter.
"Facebook's governance structure continues to put its investors at risk," Illinois State Treasurer Michael Frerichs said in a statement. "Now is the time for change. We need to see more accountability of Mark Zuckerberg to the Board of Directors to restore investor confidence and protect shareholder value."
Added Rhode Island General Treasurer Seth Magaziner: "Without an independent board chair, the board's oversight of the company remains inadequate, as evidenced by the recent mishandling of several controversies. Having an independent board chair, separate from the Mr. Zuckerberg's role as CEO, is in the best long-term interest of Facebook shareholders, including the members of Rhode Island's pension system."
The Trillium-led group said Apple ( AAPL ), Alphabet 's Google ( GOOGL ), Microsoft ( MSFT ), Oracle ( ORCL ), and Twitter ( TWTR ) have separate CEOs and chairs. Some 59% of the S&P 1,500 have similar arrangements as of April 2018, the group said.
While stinging, and yet another marker of growing distrust of the social-media giant, the proposal is unlikely to have much sway. Zuckerberg's share of voting power among company investors is roughly 60%, according to Facebook's latest proxy.
Facebook But in a proxy filing for 2017, the company noted a proposal to appoint an independent chair was voted down previously.
Still, discord could mount. In July, Facebook projected weaker-than-expected revenue growth and its shares have been battered more than 25% since then.
Facebook's next shareholder meeting is in May 2019.
